title: School Bus Crash in Johnson County
seoTitle: School Bus Crash in Johnson County Leaves 1 Dead
subtitle: An Abingdon High School bus collides with a vehicle, leaving one dead and several injured
excerpt: An Abingdon High School bus collided with a vehicle on Friday night in Johnson County, Tennessee.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
On Friday night, an Abingdon High School bus collided with a vehicle on Highway 91 in Johnson County, Tennessee. The crash left one adult dead and several injured, including students and the bus driver.

Crash Location

The collision occurred in the 7000 block of Highway 91 at around 9:35 p.m. Highway 91 was closed nearby due to the crash, according to TDOT.

Impact Details

The vehicle that collided with the bus was a Subaru driven by 35-year-old Douglas McMillian. The Subaru crossed the center line and struck the bus head-on, sending both vehicles into a ditch. The driver of the Subaru died at the scene.

Injuries and Evacuation

According to Johnson County police, 28 people were aboard the bus at the time of the crash. Three students and the bus driver were transported to the hospital with minor injuries. The accident also triggered a secondary collision, which resulted in minor injuries in another vehicle.

Response from Authorities

The Tennessee Highway Patrol (THP) and the Johnson County Sheriff's Office (JCSO) responded to the scene. The JCSO expressed gratitude to everyone involved in the rescue operation. Johnson City Medical Center and Johnston Memorial Hospital were called upon to treat the injured.

Support for the Victims

Washington County Public Schools (WCPS) and Abingdon High School issued statements thanking first responders and the community members who assisted students and staff. The release highlighted the actions of the bus drivers, coaching staff, and athletic trainers during the emergency.

Conclusion

The Friday night crash in Johnson County left one adult dead and several injured, including Abingdon High School students. The swift response from authorities and the support from the school community were essential in handling the tragedy.

With information from WCYB, WSLS.
